summary: Your report covers most mission elements and is readable, with a clear executive summary and useful STK screenshots. The main weaknesses are orbit/launch inconsistencies, contact-time misreporting, contradictory EOL logic, incomplete user/operator detail, missing software-file evidence, and weak referencing. You are in the Adequate band; to reach Accomplished, correct these technical errors and strengthen evidence and referencing.
next_steps: Correct the launch and orbit calculations: Kourou latitude, SSO inclination consistency, RAAN/launch geometry, and the feasibility/cost of the plane change or dogleg for a retrograde SSO from ~5°N.
Reconcile the ground-contact duration with the STK table and resolve the EOL contradiction between a manoeuvre, no thrusters, and a passive drag sail; include software files as evidence.
Explicitly name the operator and customers in the Introduction, and rebuild the Bibliography with full metadata, no Wikipedia, and matching in-text citations.

criteria.C1: You clearly describe the mission, rationale and single-spacecraft choice with references. To move from Adequate to Accomplished, explicitly name the operator and customers, not just implied Australian facilities/scientists, and support user roles with literature. Your Executive Summary and Introduction already provide a good base; add specific user requirements and operational responsibilities.
criteria.C2: You cover launch, orbit, ground station, duration and EOL with STK screenshots and an access table. Next level requires correcting the Kourou latitude (45.05°N vs ~5.2°N), making the 600 km SSO inclination consistent (~97.8° retrograde, not 87.79°), assessing the plane-change/dogleg, correcting mean contact time (580.786 s ≈9.7 min, not almost 20), resolving the EOL manoeuvre/thruster/drag-sail contradiction, and evidencing software files.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion summarises launch, orbit and ground-station choices, but it is generic and omits meaningful conclusions on mission duration and EOL. To reach Accomplished, draw specific conclusions from your evidence: state how the chosen orbit/launch/ground segment meet mission needs, justify the unbuilt Vega E with a clearer fallback, and include duration/EOL outcomes rather than only restating choices.
criteria.C4: Your structure, headings and executive summary are clear and readable. To reach Accomplished, make figure/table numbering and captions consistent (e.g. Image 1/Image 4), provide full bibliography metadata (titles, authors, access dates) instead of bare URLs, remove Wikipedia, and ensure every in-text citation matches the reference list. These changes will lift presentation from readable to professional.
